output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error on our side. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation suite, the mandarin product record was copied from avocados, so it carries a 7.0°C carriage temperature instead of our 4.0°C specification. All five Meridane containers were sent with that 7.0°C setpoint, and the carrier's controllers held it closely. All five were rejected. Every container at 4.0°C passed. That includes Coastway containers and the early Meridane container, and it includes containers packed with the new fungicide. So the fungicide, Meridane's equipment and the transit time are not the cause. Lower Serra fruit did show more decay within rejected containers, but it was 28–40% of every container. The data can't show that this fruit caused the rejections. I'm about 90% sure of the main finding. Next steps: correct the product record to 4.0°C now. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check of reefer settings against the product spec before submission. Don't suspend Lower Serra, file the cargo claim, switch fungicide back, or penalise the contractor yet. Loggers in containers are a reasonable extra safeguard.
